---
title: "Tasks native Start on Vite+ and Cloudflare"
description: "How the native Tasks candidate is built on the start bridge, and what it does and does not yet cover."
---

Tasks has a native TanStack Start candidate built through
[`@tuturuuu/start-bridge`](/build/devops/start-bridge). `next build` (package
`build`) remains the production path on Vercel. The native build is
`build:cloudflare` and nothing publishes it; production stays held until an
explicit cutover PR.

## Layout

| Piece | File |
| --- | --- |
| Route registries | `start-bridge.routes.json` generates `src/runtime/*.bridge.gen.ts`; `bun run routes:check` fails on drift |
| Worker entry | `cloudflare/worker.ts` → `src/runtime/worker-handler.ts` (bridge handler, build-info, runtime tag, noindex) |
| Pages | `src/routes/$.tsx` loads `src/runtime/page-model.server.ts`, one loader per manifest pattern (`satisfies Record<PagePattern, …>`), rendered by `page-view.tsx` |
| Workspace shell | `workspace-model.server.ts` (the `[wsId]` layout guards as data) and `workspace-view.tsx` |
| Server actions | `src/runtime/action-ports.ts` replaces client-reached `'use server'` modules with server functions in the native build only; each server half re-checks the actor |
| Types | `tsconfig.json` (Next) excludes the native files; `tsconfig.native.json` covers them. `type-check` runs both |

`build-info` is owned by the Worker. The `serwist/[path]` route builds the
offline worker with esbuild at request time and stays on the Next build until
the native offline port; the native shell does not register a service worker.

## Build notes

- Run Vite with `--configLoader runner` (the package scripts do). The bridge's
  `vite` preset is TypeScript with extensionless imports, which the default
  native-ESM config loader cannot load.
- The Worker (`ssr`) bundle sets rolldown `strictExecutionOrder`: circular
  server chunks otherwise ran a CommonJS interop wrapper before its chunk
  initialized and the Worker failed at startup.
- `debug` and `supports-color` 7 are CommonJS and `require('tty')` in their Node
  entry, which cannot run in the ESM Worker. A resolve plugin uses each
  package's own `browser` entry; ESM releases with `exports` maps are untouched.
- Proxy rewrites (crawler link preview, root fallback) reach the page loader
  through the `x-tuturuuu-page-rewrite` request header, because the bridge
  renders the browser-visible URL. The Worker strips any client-sent copy.
- The server reads Supabase public configuration from Worker vars at runtime
  (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`); build
  environment only reaches the client bundle.

## Mounts

One artifact serves `tasks.tuturuuu.com` at its root and `tuturuuu.com/tasks`
as a mount (`TASKS_MOUNTS` in `worker-handler.ts`); the bridge resolves the
base per request, so assets, server functions and redirects follow the host.
Outside the mount the apex answers 404. Cookies are not renamed or
path-scoped: Tasks uses the one shared Tuturuuu session. Every native
response carries `x-tuturuuu-runtime: native` for post-cutover attribution.
The staging profile (`void.config.ts`, `tuturuuu-tasks-vite-staging`) sets
`TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=1`.

Cutover is direct (no staged canary): exact-head gates, cross-family review
and a staging smoke where staging exists, then the flip with the prior Vercel
deployment and captured routing ready as a one-step rollback, a post-deploy
smoke and a 30–60 minute watch.

## Local emitted smoke

On a Studio host, after `bun run build:cloudflare`, run the emitted Worker in
local workerd with loopback-only fixtures:

```bash
bunx wrangler dev --config dist/server/wrangler.json --ip 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 18797 --local \
  --var NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL:http://127.0.0.1:54321 \
  --var NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY:sb_publishable_fixture_only
```

Check `/api/build-info`, a static file, an unauthenticated page (redirect to
the central login with a `verify-token` return URL), an API route without a
session (401), the server-function base (415 for a non-JSON POST) and the
runtime header. Probe the mount with `Host: tuturuuu.com` and `/tasks/...` paths
against the same artifact. This smoke does not replace exact-commit CI, sealed-artifact
checks or signed-in acceptance on staging.

## Shared Calendar task ports

The Calendar task model and view live in `packages/tasks-ui/tu-do/shared`.
The model receives headers, navigation and workspace permission services
from its framework adapter. Its portable entrypoint imports no request
globals or framework navigation APIs. Calendar's previous paths remain
small adapters and re-exports.

`createAuthorizedWorkspaceReader` checks the injected actor before reading
workspaces. Each app keeps its own compiled server-function entry and
supplies its registered satellite identity. Do not share a server function
that selects its app audience from client input.

Use the shared scheduling transport and notification view instead of app
copies. The existing shared workspace invitation card remains the client
entry for invitation rendering.
